title: Anticipatory slot prefetch & KV-hysteresis tuning for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed-turn traffic (short prompts followed by long responses and vice versa) causes KV-residency churn and GPU slab fragmentation under the continuous batching scheduler. Over-provisioning KV slots reduces tail latency but increases average memory pressure and copy overhead; under-provisioning forces frequent eviction and re-population, hurting P95/P99 latency and costing extra GPU cycles.

Proposal: Implement an "anticipatory slot prefetch" mechanism with a KV-hysteresis window and lightweight turn-length predictor to reduce thrashing while keeping end-to-end latency SLOs. Key components:
- Turn-probing predictor: online, per-session histogram + small logistic classifier (features: recent response lengths, token generation rate, model variant, route) to predict next-response token budget (fast path, <1ms per request).
- Prefetch reservation: proactively reserve a small number of KV slots when predictor indicates a likely long response; reservations allocate KV residency budget but remain soft (evictable) until generation begins.
- Hysteresis window: a time-based and token-based hysteresis prevents immediate un-reservation/re-reservation for oscillating patterns; parameters: time_hz_ms and token_hz_count.
- Residency budgets: per-customer/route soft quotas (fairness) integrated with existing slab allocator to avoid noisy-neighbor eviction.
- Admission controls: back-pressure on prefetched slots when GPU free memory < threshold; notify scheduler to switch to short-path kernels if prefetch cannot be satisfied.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- P95 latency for long-response flows reduced by >= 15% vs baseline continuous scheduler while keeping P99 within -5% of baseline.
- Overall GPU memory fragmentation score reduced by >= 10% (measured by free-slab-run variance metric).
- No customer exceeds its residency budget more than 0.5% of requests in steady state.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike: build predictor prototype (Ayesha) and simulator against production sampling trace (2 days).
2) Scheduler integration: add reservation APIs + hysteresis knobs (Jonah) (5 days).
3) Canary: deploy to 10% of low-risk routes with extended metrics and tracing (2 days).
4) Analysis: run 2-week A/B, validate metrics, tune hysteresis/time constants (team).
5) Rollout: staged increase to 50% then 100% with rollback gates based on P99/regression alarms.

Rollout gates and rollback criteria:
- Immediate rollback if P99 increases > 8% for any customer in canary cohort.
- Throttle prefetch admitted rate if GPU average free memory < 6% for >10m.

Notes: This approach trades small predictive logic and a tiny amount of soft-reserved memory for significantly fewer cold-KV refills. We must carefully tune the predictor threshold to avoid prefetch storms for highly bursty short-turn patterns.
